newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine government hails deal with unions.
newsitem.headline: Argentine government hails deal with unions.

text.p: Argentina's government on Saturday hailed a deal with unions which it hopes will head off a planned general strike, but a hard-line union and a small- business group challenged the agreement.

Cabinet chief Jorge Rodriguez called the agreement in principle struck Friday with the main labour federation CGT a "very positive" development which should help reduce unemployment now standing at 17.3 percent.

"We hope that the agreements between government and unions will have the support of the business sector so that we can make headway in labour legislation modernisation, which is a very important step towards improving work access for Argentines," he told a local radio station.

The CGT has said that, if formally approved by the Group of Eight main business lobbies -- which has already endorsed it informally -- it might ditch its plans to call for a general strike sometime this month.
But the hard-line Argentine Workers Center (CTA) called the deal, which reportedly includes an agreement to cut severance payment by 30 percent, unacceptable.
"It is inadmissible that such a deal would not tackle the problem of unemployment," it said in a press release.

The Business Unit Council of Buenos Aires, which groups small entreprises in Argentina's main industrial belt, complained it was shut out of tripartite talks between the government, the CGT and the Group of Eight.

"The agreement cannot and should not take only into account the interests of the big corporations while ignoring the small enterprises which are the main sources of jobs in the country," the Council said in a press release.
"The Group of Eight does not represent us."

The government proposes swapping redundancy payouts for unemployment insurance and allowing workers to make salary and labour condition deals directly with employers with no centralised union intervention. It is also pushing for a complete deregulation of the union-controlled private health system.
